text.p: Wheat, gold and copper prices strengthened, while oil prices eased among Australian-interest commodities. The CRB index ended on Friday up 0.83 at 248.27.
Base metal markets ended a less-active Friday LME session generally steadier, with copper and aluminium showing strong gains at the end of the kerb.

Traders said the markets absorbed the expected booksquaring ahead of the weekend, with copper in particular bracing itself for the fiercely tight nearby prompts that fall due from next Monday. Conditions picked up towards the close on shortcovering and prices ended around their peaks.

In copper, the cash/threes spread was around $200/210, near its highs of the week with the tightness likely to be maintained next week and cash/one day rates seen flaring. The forward market closed at $2,383, up $15 a tonne, signalling another challenge of $2,400. The labour disputes at Escondida, Quebrada Branca and Phelps Dodge, as well as the maintainance shutdown of
Kennecott's smelter remained the fundamental props.

Aluminium performed strongly, and looks to have built a base above $1,600. Borrowing of early July to the July date helped the trend also, and pulled cash/threes into $25/27 contango. Last three months business was at $1,613, up $19 from Thursday's close. Alloy was marked up and ended at $1,490/95 a tonne.
Solid fundamentals helped zinc, with last business at $1,275, up $4, while tin and nickel followed the trend, closing at $5,740 and $7,480, respective gains of $20 and $30.
However, sluggish physicals and rising stocks inhibited lead, which closed at $631, down $4.

Renewed concerns about harsh weather in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region and a rally in soybeans boosted CBOT wheat futures to higher closes, traders said. Support also came from ideas more rain is needed in dry European areas to stem further deterioration of wheat there. Wheat closed unchanged to nine cents per bushel higher, with July up 6-1/2 at $4.32-1/4.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher Friday, but volumes were again light, with the focus on gains in the platinum metals group. COMEX June gold ended up $1.20 an ounce at $343.90, after another unsuccessful test of the top of the $340-345 range of the past two weeks. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $341.90/40, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $342.25 and the New York close Thursday around $340.50/00.

NYMEX crude ended lower Friday after late session gains on crude output disruptions in Nigeria failed to break technical resistance, traders said. June crude ended off four cents at $19.99 a barrel. Spot crude rose as high as $20.22, failing to break resistance of $20.27, June crude's high for the week. Royal Dutch Shell Group said it had to close its Warri flow station last weekend due to renewed clashes in the oil-producing swamps between militant youths in Nigeria.

CSCE world sugar futures closed firmer and near session highs as prices retraced some of the losses made during the previous session. Trading sources said many players kept to the sidelines in the wake of huge price swings in the past week and before the last trading day for May sugar on April 30. The most-active July contract traded from a high of 11.37 cents a lb hit on Wednesday to a low of 10.91 cents Thursday.
